title: Month 11
subtitle: The twelve-month visit is next month, and it is the one with the most decisions in it.

baby.development: Your baby is standing, may be taking first steps, and can say one or two words. They understand no and can follow a simple instruction.

you.body: If you are breastfeeding, you may be down to morning and night feeds. If you are formula feeding, you are close to the end of it.
you.mind: Eleven months is when the first birthday planning starts, and when the twelve-month visit questions start to matter. Write them down now.

coreActions.title: Book the twelve-month visit
coreActions.why: This is the visit with the most decisions: vaccines, the switch to whole milk, and the developmental check.
coreActions.detail: The US schedule at twelve months is MMR, varicella, Hib, and PCV, and hepatitis A and B depending on what was given earlier. Ask about whole milk, iron, and whether the baby needs a lead test. Ask about walking if they are not yet.

coreActions.title: Plan the switch to whole milk
coreActions.why: The switch is a change of habit as much as a change of drink, and doing it over a week is easier than doing it overnight.
coreActions.detail: Whole milk from twelve months, two to three cups a day, in an open cup. Mix it with formula over a week if the baby refuses it. Do not add it to a bottle at bedtime, because that is the habit that causes tooth decay.

coreActions.title: Give the baby something to push
coreActions.why: A push toy gives a baby who is not yet confident the balance to take steps.
coreActions.detail: A sturdy push wagon or a laundry basket with something heavy in it. Not a baby walker with wheels and a seat, which is banned in Canada and associated with injuries here.

alsoKnow.title: Ask about a lead test
alsoKnow.body: The CDC recommends a blood lead test for children at twelve months in many areas, and the pediatrician will know whether yours is one. Lead has no symptoms at low levels.

alsoKnow.title: Drop the bottle by twelve months
alsoKnow.body: Prolonged bottle use is linked to tooth decay and to iron deficiency from too much milk. Twelve months is the usual time to move to an open cup and a straw cup.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
Fast or labored breathing, or a blue tint around the lips
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
